title: Goal Misgeneralization Detection: Can Monitors Distinguish Capability Failure from Deceptive Alignment?
original_idea: Construct 20 paired scenarios where the same bad outcome is caused by either genuine incapability or deliberate under-performance. Evaluate whether a standard LLM monitor can distinguish these cases with appropriate prompts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Addresses one of the central challenges of AI oversight: distinguishing deceptive alignment from genuine incapability. Even negative results (monitors cannot distinguish) would be highly safety-relevant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing 20 paired scenarios that convincingly separate incapability from deliberate under-performance is very challenging. Requires deep understanding of agent capabilities and deceptive alignment. Beginner CS students would struggle to create convincing scenarios in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The 20 paired scenarios create a large design space. Each scenario pair needs careful construction. The experiment itself (run monitor, measure accuracy) is narrow, but the scenario construction is broad and subjective.
